methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $14M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
The ePlane Company is a Series B transportation-sector venture that has raised $14M+ and is currently fundraising $40–50M. The broader transportation sector comp universe consists of eight private peers (including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, and Parallel Systems) and zero public comparables; however, no narrowly-matched same-stage or adjacent-stage peers exist with sufficient data density to support a reliable peer-median valuation.

Given data constraints, only the stage-progression method is applicable. Using total raised ($14M) as a proxy for Series A valuation and applying a typical 1.9x step-up multiplier for the Series B progression yields an implied valuation of $27M. This method assumes the target's capital efficiency and growth trajectory align with sector norms; deviations would materially shift the result.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $23M (low) to $31M (median $27M), derived entirely from stage-progression mechanics rather than peer triangulation. Key uncertainties include the company's actual Series A post-money valuation (used as a proxy here), the appropriateness of the 1.9x multiplier given frontier-tech operational risk, and competitive positioning relative to the broader transportation cohort. A fuller peer-based methodology will require identification of additional comparable Series B or Series C transportation ventures with disclosed valuation data.
